source.title: Illumination at the Moon's South Pole, 2023 to 2030
source.organization: NASA Scientific Visualization Studio (Goddard Space Flight Center)
source.credits: Visualizer: Ernie Wright (STC). Scientist: Noah Petro (NASA/GSFC). Technical support: Laurence Schuler, Ian Jones (ADNET Systems).
dataUsed: LRO LOLA digital elevation model (SVS dataset 653)

relatedProduct.title: Illumination at the Moon's South Pole to 80°S, 2025 to 2028
relatedProduct.whyNotSampled: Same team, method and inputs, but crater names are printed over the map and the 'Shackleton' label covers the SELENE-1 site; scale ~0.57 km/px vs ~0.11 km/px in SVS 4930.

observationContext: Model-based visualization, not a direct observation: sunlight and shadow are ray-traced over measured LOLA terrain for the Sun positions given by the DE421 ephemeris. It is a prediction for 2026, valid for the terrain resolution of the rendering.

site.name: SELENE-1 (fictional base) at the LOLA best-lit pixel near Shackleton crater

method.timeCheck: On-screen time labels checked: frame 1 = 01 Jan 2026 00:00 UT, frame 2000 = 16 Jun 2026 14:00 UT, frame 4380 = 31 Dec 2026 22:00 UT.
method.projection: Orthographic polar view centred on the pole; 88°S ring measured at 539.5 px (≈269.8 px per degree, ≈0.11 km per px); Shackleton centre predicted at the crater's rim centre.
method.variable: sunlitFraction = share of the day's twelve 2-hour frames in which the site's 3×3-pixel median luminance is above the threshold (0..1)

limitations: Derived from rendered visualization frames, not from a published numeric data product.
Lit/shadow is binary per 2-hour frame; partial Sun-disc visibility and shadow edges are not resolved.
One pixel ≈ 110 m, coarser than the 60 m LOLA illumination map; a 3×3 block (~330 m) is sampled.
Only the Sun is modelled; Earth-shine, panel height above ground and panel orientation are ignored.
Sunlit fraction is not electrical power: converting it to kWh uses game assumptions (panel size, performance).
